beats.text: Lindbergh was not the first to fly nonstop across the Atlantic.
beats.note: He flew solo from New York to Paris in over 33 hours and won the $25,000 Orteig Prize. Two men had crossed nonstop eight years earlier.

beats.text: Alcock and Brown left Newfoundland in a converted bomber.
beats.note: They took off from Lester's Field near St John's at about 1:45 p.m. in a modified First World War Vickers Vimy.

beats.context: About how long the crossing took, 1,890 miles from Newfoundland to Ireland.

beats.text: They landed nose first in a bog.
beats.note: They aimed for what looked like a green field near Clifden, County Galway. It was Derrigimlagh Bog. The aircraft nosed over and neither man was hurt.
It was offered for a crossing in under 72 consecutive hours. A week later both men were knighted at Windsor Castle.
He was killed on 18 December 1919 near Rouen, flying a new Vickers Viking amphibian to the Paris Airshow.

beats.text: The first nonstop crossing came eight years before the famous one.

beats.line: Check who was first before you repeat it.
